page.layout: One printed page (page 270) with a main text column in the centre and a narrow column of marginal notes along the right margin. Running head at top above the text. Digitiser's banner at the bottom is excluded.

main_text.p: sio priore sit longior, & vehemen-tior, citiusque recurrat; morbus citò admodum ad statum veniet. Sin con-tra se res habeat, ita ut posterior ac-cessio sit priore brevior, benignior, tardiusque redeat; morbus declinat, vigorque & status superati sunt. At-que hęc quidem intelligenda sunt de morbo periodos habente; quibus si careat, ad symptomatum incremen-tum decurrendum est. hæc enim si celeriter augeantur, brevi status ex-pectandus: Quod dico, evidens est in morbis à causis calidis, qui citò moventur. Sin causa sit frigida; con-trarium fiet. Huc referuntur anni tempus, regio, ætas, natura ægri &c. Iuvenis enim, in regione calida, æſta-te, si ægrotet; ut plurimum morbus celerem habebit statum. An tempora morborum, æqualiter & inæquali-ter (nimirum an principium sit ve-lox, augmentum tardum vel contra constanter, ordinatè; an vero contra disces non tantum ex propriis symp-tomatis, sed & supervenientibus ac-ciden-

page.notes: Marginal notes on the right edge are largely cut off and only partly legible (fragments such as "Inveni", "benignis", "in maiio", "symptomatu", "res primi", "Status"); they are not transcribed. The text of the last line "ciden-" continues onto the following page. Some words in the main text at the right edge are slightly obscured by the binding shadow and the margin notes.
